## Load data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(mgcv)

train <- read_csv("data-train.csv")
```

```{r}
train <- train |>
  mutate(
    m1 = R_moment_1, m2 = R_moment_2,
    m3 = R_moment_3, m4 = R_moment_4,

    # Central moments
    C_moment_2 = m2 - m1^2,
    C_moment_3 = m3 - 3*m1*m2 + 2*m1^3,
    C_moment_4 = m4 - 4*m1*m3 + 6*m1^2*m2 - 3*m1^4,

    # Summary statistics
    sd_R = sqrt(C_moment_2),
    skewness = C_moment_3 / sd_R^3,
    kurtosis = C_moment_4 / sd_R^4,
    ex_kurt = kurtosis - 3,

    # Keep infinite Fr as a valid category
    Fr = as.factor(Fr),
    Re = as.factor(Re)
  )
```

## Mean spline model

```{r}
model_mean <- gam(
  log(R_moment_1) ~ Re + Fr + s(St, k = 5),
  data = train,
  method = "REML"
)
```

```{r}
summary(model_mean)
plot(model_mean, shade = TRUE)
gam.check(model_mean)
```

## LOOCV

```{r}
predict_original <- function(model, newdata) {
  smearing_factor <- mean(exp(residuals(model, type = "response")))
  exp(predict(model, newdata = newdata)) * smearing_factor
}

loocv_predict <- function(model, data) {
  map_dbl(seq_len(nrow(data)), function(i) {
    fold_model <- update(model, data = data[-i, ])
    predict_original(fold_model, data[i, ])
  })
}

predictions <- train |>
  mutate(
    pred_mean = loocv_predict(model_mean, train),
    pred_sd = loocv_predict(model_sd, train),
    pred_skewness = loocv_predict(model_skewness, train),
    pred_kurtosis = loocv_predict(model_kurtosis, train)
  )
```

```{r}
score_predictions <- function(response, observed, predicted) {
  tibble(
    Response = response,
    RMSE = sqrt(mean((observed - predicted)^2)),
    MAE = mean(abs(observed - predicted))
  )
}

performance <- bind_rows(
  score_predictions("Mean", predictions$R_moment_1, predictions$pred_mean),
  score_predictions("Standard deviation", predictions$sd_R, predictions$pred_sd),
  score_predictions("Skewness", predictions$skewness, predictions$pred_skewness),
  score_predictions("Kurtosis", predictions$kurtosis, predictions$pred_kurtosis)
)
```

## Prediction performance summary

```{r}
knitr::kable(
  performance,
  digits = c(0, 4, 5),
  format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  caption = "Spline model performance using LOOCV"
)
```

## Observed versus predicted: all four responses

```{r}
compare_response <- function(label, observed, predicted) {
  tibble(
    Response = label,
    St = predictions$St, Re = predictions$Re, Fr = predictions$Fr,
    Observed = observed,
    Predicted = predicted,
    Absolute_error = abs(predicted - observed)
  )
}

comparison_data <- bind_rows(
  compare_response("Mean", predictions$R_moment_1, predictions$pred_mean),
  compare_response("Standard deviation", predictions$sd_R, predictions$pred_sd),
  compare_response("Skewness", predictions$skewness, predictions$pred_skewness),
  compare_response("Kurtosis", predictions$kurtosis, predictions$pred_kurtosis)
)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6
ggplot(comparison_data, aes(x = Observed, y = Predicted)) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(aes(color = Fr), size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~Response, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "Observed response", y = "Held-out prediction", color = "Fr") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Spline models predict mean cluster volume more successfully than the other three responses using LOOCV.

Many large skewness and kurtosis errors occur at `Fr` = 0.052.

## Extension: separate St curves by Fr

**Sd**

```{r}
model_sd_fr_train <- gam(
  log(sd_R) ~ Re + Fr + s(St, by = Fr, k = 5),
  data = train,
  method = "REML"
)

summary(model_sd_fr_train)
plot(model_sd_fr_train, shade = TRUE, pages = 1)
gam.check(model_sd_fr_train)
```

```{r}
sd_fr_prediction <- loocv_predict(model_sd_fr_train, train)

sd_model_comparison <- bind_rows(
  score_predictions("Shared St curve", train$sd_R,
                    predictions$pred_sd),
  score_predictions("Fr-specific St curves", train$sd_R,
                    sd_fr_prediction)
) |>
  rename(Model = Response)

knitr::kable(sd_model_comparison, digits = 2,
             caption = "Standard deviation: baseline versus Fr-specific curves")
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
sd_plot_data <- bind_rows(
  tibble(Model = "Shared St curve", Observed = train$sd_R,
         Predicted = predictions$pred_sd, Fr = train$Fr),
  tibble(Model = "Fr-specific St curves", Observed = train$sd_R,
         Predicted = sd_fr_prediction, Fr = train$Fr)
)

ggplot(sd_plot_data, aes(Observed, Predicted, color = Fr)) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~Model) +
  labs(x = "Observed standard deviation", y = "Held-out prediction") +
  theme_minimal()
```

**Kurtosis**

```{r}
model_kurtosis_fr_train <- gam(
  log(kurtosis) ~ Re + Fr + s(St, by = Fr, k = 5),
  data = train,
  method = "REML"
)

summary(model_kurtosis_fr_train)
plot(model_kurtosis_fr_train, shade = TRUE, pages = 1)
gam.check(model_kurtosis_fr_train)
```

```{r}
kurtosis_fr_prediction <- loocv_predict(model_kurtosis_fr_train, train)

kurtosis_model_comparison <- bind_rows(
  score_predictions("Shared St curve", train$kurtosis,
                    predictions$pred_kurtosis),
  score_predictions("Fr-specific St curves", train$kurtosis,
                    kurtosis_fr_prediction)
) |>
  rename(Model = Response)

knitr::kable(kurtosis_model_comparison, digits = 2,
             caption = "Kurtosis: baseline versus Fr-specific curves")
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
kurtosis_plot_data <- bind_rows(
  tibble(Model = "Shared St curve", Observed = train$kurtosis,
         Predicted = predictions$pred_kurtosis, Fr = train$Fr),
  tibble(Model = "Fr-specific St curves", Observed = train$kurtosis,
         Predicted = kurtosis_fr_prediction, Fr = train$Fr)
)

ggplot(kurtosis_plot_data, aes(Observed, Predicted, color = Fr)) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~Model) +
  labs(x = "Observed kurtosis", y = "Held-out prediction") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Under LOOCV, Fr-specific curves still have higher RMSE and MAE for SD and skewness. For kurtosis, they modestly improve both metrics: RMSE decreases from about 152,604 to 147,246 and MAE from 81,908 to 80,625.

-   Mean predictions track observed values reasonably well.

-   Large standard deviations are still underpredicted.

-   Skewness and kurtosis still have substantial prediction errors.
